extra.message: The 'host' GET parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system() ('ping -c 1 ' + host). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(...)`) to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

The 'fragment' GET parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered with Template(...).render(). This allows Server-Side Template Injection, letting an attacker execute arbitrary Python code via Jinja2 template syntax (e.g. {{ self.__init__.__globals__ ... }}), leading to remote code execution.

etree.XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True (and no_network=False) and used to parse raw request.body. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, allowing an attacker to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via crafted XML with external entity references.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The request JSON body ('filter' key, or the whole payload) is passed directly as the MongoDB query filter to find_one() with no validation or sanitization. An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. {"$where": ...} or {"$ne": null}) to bypass intended query logic or extract unauthorized data (NoSQL injection).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The 'name' GET parameter is used unsanitized to build a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and the raw request body is written to it. Since 'name' is not validated against path traversal sequences (e.g. '../../etc/cron.d/x'), an attacker can write arbitrary files outside the intended export directory.

Unlike every other handler in this file, patient_identity_ping_339 never calls _wrk_gate(request) to verify the internal ops token before processing the request. This endpoint is reachable by any unauthenticated caller, unlike its siblings which all require a valid X-Internal-Token header.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The Origin request header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint, defeating the same-origin policy and enabling cross-site data theft using victim cookies/credentials.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Authorization decision ('elevated' lane exposing payroll/casework data) is based on a client-supplied cookie ('ops_badge') or header ('x-ops-badge') value equal to 'lead'. Since this value is fully attacker-controlled (a cookie can be freely set by the client) and not tied to any server-side session or signature, an attacker can trivially set this cookie/header to escalate privileges.

The 'amount' subtracted from the ledger balance and the resulting 'state' (e.g. 'approved') are taken directly from the client-supplied JSON body/query string with no validation or authorization check on the values. A caller can set an arbitrary amount (including negative, increasing balance) and force state to 'approved' regardless of any real approval workflow.

The client-supplied JSON body (change_set) is merged directly into the workset dict via dict.update() with no field whitelist. This allows an attacker to override sensitive fields such as 'is_admin' and 'credit_limit' that were not meant to be client-controlled (mass assignment).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: User-supplied 'expr' GET parameter is passed to eval(). Although __builtins__ is restricted to {}, this is a known-insufficient sandbox: attacker-controlled expressions can still escape restricted eval via object introspection (e.g. via ''.__class__.__mro__ ...) to reach dangerous builtins, leading to arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: The 'lane' parameter from GET or POST is passed directly to redirect() with no validation that it is a local/relative path. An attacker can supply a full external URL (e.g. //evil.com or https://evil.com) to redirect victims to an attacker-controlled site (open redirect, useful for phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: The 'copyline' GET parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML string and returned as an HttpResponse with content_type text/html, with no escaping. An attacker can inject HTML/JavaScript (e.g. <script>...</script>) that executes in the victim's browser (reflected XSS).

The full raw request body and the Authorization header value are written to the application log at WARNING level via logger.warning(). This can leak credentials, bearer tokens, and PHI/PII contained in the request into log files/aggregators, which typically have weaker access controls than the application itself.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The response embeds a hardcoded live-looking secret token ('tok_live_partner_sync' as 'sync_key') and an SSN-shaped value ('739-44-1982' as 'tax_ref') that are returned to any caller possessing the internal token. Hardcoded secrets in source and unguarded exposure of PII-shaped data in an API response are both sensitive-data-exposure risks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: A dictionary of hardcoded verifier/PIN values ('north': '4812', 'south': '5930') is embedded directly in source code and used as the sole authentication check for the endpoint.

The user-supplied 'verifier' is compared to the expected secret using standard string '!=' comparison, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. This timing difference can be measured by an attacker to recover the secret verifier byte-by-byte (timing side-channel).

The internal ops token comparison (request.headers.get('x-internal-token') == gate_value), which gates nearly every endpoint in this file, uses a non-constant-time '==' comparison instead of hmac.compare_digest(). This can allow a timing side-channel attack to recover the valid token value.
The handler explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and clears the Content-Security-Policy header to an empty string, disabling browser-level XSS mitigations for responses from this endpoint.

ssl._create_unverified_context() disables TLS certificate verification (and hostname checking) before making an outbound HTTPS request to a partner endpoint, making the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

DEBUG defaults to True ('1') when the DJANGO_DEBUG environment variable is not set. If this default reaches a production deployment, Django will display detailed stack traces, source code, and settings values to users on error, leaking sensitive internal information.

SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'dev-only-change-me' if DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is not set in the environment. If deployed without overriding this variable, session/CSRF signing and password-reset tokens rely on a publicly-known secret, allowing session forgery and token prediction.
